title: Writing the max loop
idea: TOOL: assemble the best-so-far loop piece by piece. Light code, with predictable results.

exercises.prompt: Tap the tokens to set the starting best to the first value of nums.
exercises.explanation: best = nums[0] starts the champion at the first real value so comparisons work even for negatives.

exercises.prompt:
Write the loop header that visits each value in nums (call the value n):

for ____ in nums:
exercises.explanation: 'for n in nums:' takes each value one at a time into n.

exercises.prompt:
Write the test that is true when n beats the best so far:

    if n ____ best:
exercises.explanation: n > best is true exactly when n is bigger, which is when you should replace best.

exercises.prompt:
Write the line that saves the new winner into best:

        best ____ n
exercises.explanation: best = n stores the bigger value. (Remember: winner goes INTO best, not the other way round.)

exercises.prompt: Put the whole max program in order.
exercises.explanation: Start best, loop, test, replace on a win, print the final biggest.

exercises.prompt: You assembled the loop for nums = [6, 2, 9, 4]. What prints?
exercises.explanation: best climbs 6 -> 9 and nothing beats 9. It prints the maximum, 9.

exercises.prompt: Tap the tokens to print the result after the loop.
exercises.explanation: print(best) shows the biggest value once the loop has finished walking every item.

exercises.prompt: Where must 'best = n' sit so it only runs on a winning value?
options: At the same level as the for
exercises.explanation: Indenting it under the if ties the replacement to the comparison, so it only runs when n is bigger.

exercises.prompt: The loop variable name (n, t, s, value) does not change what the code does, as long as you use it consistently.
exercises.explanation: Any name works; pick one that reads well. Just use the SAME name in the loop header and inside the loop.

exercises.prompt: After you build it, what is the best next step before trusting it?
options: Trace it by hand on a small list and compare to the output
Run it on a million numbers
exercises.explanation: Hand-tracing a small list gives you an expected answer to check the code against — the Check habit.
